comparator.name: Business Administration (Bedrijfskunde)
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026–27 curriculum accounts for exactly 180 ECTS: 60 compulsory ECTS in year 1, 60 compulsory ECTS in year 2, and a third year with 30 ECTS of genuine choice space plus 18 ECTS of fixed courses and a 12-ECTS thesis. The genuine third-year choice may be exchange, a 24-ECTS internship plus a 6-ECTS elective, Economics and Management minors, or another Tilburg minor; it is preserved as open space rather than populated to improve UCR overlap. Zero-credit GROW development is excluded from the 180-ECTS total.
components: Genuine 30-ECTS choice space; no specific elective content is invented.

core: Organisation, strategy, leadership and human-resource management
Accounting, finance, investment and economics for business
Marketing, entrepreneurship and applied business decisions
Operations, supply chains and process improvement
Data analysis, programming and management information systems
Business research, law, ethics, sustainability and thesis work
adjacent: Business analytics, digital systems and operational decision-making
questions: How do organisations make strategic, financial, marketing and people decisions?
How can data, digital systems and process analysis improve business performance?
How can firms combine entrepreneurship and performance with sustainability and ethics?

alternatives.label: Business management, strategy & organisational decisions
alternatives.concept: A broad closest feasible Business Administration programme combining strategy, marketing, accounting, finance, economics, organisations, leadership, entrepreneurship, research and data-informed decision-making.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum spans management, strategy, marketing, finance, economics, leadership, entrepreneurship, research and data without claiming a narrow functional specialisation.
progression: Business, economics, data, research, leadership and communication foundations precede advanced strategy, marketing, organisational psychology, econometrics, market research and international governance. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Business analytics, digital systems & operations
alternatives.concept: A business route organised around analytics, digital systems and operational decisions, joining programming, databases, data science and AI to strategy, marketing, economics, finance and entrepreneurship.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines business and entrepreneurship with programming, databases, data science, machine learning and algorithmic decision tools.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces substantial leadership, finance, qualitative-research and entrepreneurship content with programming, databases, linear algebra, probability, algorithms, machine learning, deep learning and AI ethics. Ten of the 24 courses differ, and digital analytics becomes the programme's organising logic.
progression: Business, programming, data, research and mathematical foundations precede advanced strategy, algorithms, machine learning, deep learning, international business and market research. Mathematical Methods precedes linear algebra, probability and deep learning; programming precedes algorithms. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Responsible entrepreneurship & sustainable organisations
alternatives.concept: A business route organised around responsible entrepreneurship and sustainable organisational change, combining management, economics, marketing, leadership and research with climate, circular economy, environmental governance and ethics.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum joins business, entrepreneurship and leadership to a sustained sequence in sustainability, circular economy, governance and ethics.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad and digital routes, this curriculum gives sustained weight to climate, circular economy, sustainability science, ecological innovation, environmental governance, remediation and renewable-system design. Ten courses differ from the closest programme and fourteen from the digital route, making responsible and sustainable entrepreneurship the governing academic direction.
progression: Sustainability Essentials I precedes Sustainability Essentials II, which precedes advanced circular-resource and renewable-system work; business and research foundations precede advanced law, public economics, leadership and market research, with all formal prerequisites completed earlier.

candidates.label: Business analytics, digital systems and operations

selection.assessment: The closest match covers the broad management, strategy, marketing, finance, organisational-decision and economics core. A digital-operations cluster and a responsible-entrepreneurship cluster each have direct programme-interest support, a coherent UCR curriculum and pairwise differences above the 30-ECTS floor. Three alternatives is the maximum, and every generator-eligible row is owned exactly once.

notes.text: Tilburg prescribes a dense two-year sequence across accounting, finance, marketing, operations, supply chains, human resources, business systems and research, followed by 30 ECTS of genuine choice and a 12-ECTS thesis. UCR can build coherent business, digital-analytics and responsible-enterprise curricula but does not reproduce Tilburg’s dedicated supply-chain sequence, short applied-business modules or a compulsory business thesis.
